title: service-messaging: inbox titles are frozen in the recipient's stored locale at delivery, so a zh-CN reader with no saved locale sees English notification titles
body:
domain:server#2 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufziCTpjnYbdh76SAWwb

Filing gate: ④ a per-layer child of #32218 (item 1 there: approval notification titles), split out because the fix lands in `service-messaging`, not in `plugin-approvals`. #32218's own gate is ④ under #32158, which is ③ (the maintainer's 「立卡处理」 on the 2026-11-10 full-platform test run). Measured by #32218's card thread on `origin/main` `b6fc8908`.
Business reason: every zh-CN console user whose account has no saved locale (the showcase admin, for example) reads English notification titles ("Approval requested") in a Chinese console. It affects every producer that notifies through the inbox, not only approvals.
Reader: the next `domain:server` seat that claims it. The fix lands in `packages/services/service-messaging`.
Dedupe (open AND closed): `sys_inbox_message keyedText locale` (0 hits); #24978 and #25015 (closed) are about emit-time keyed text, not read-time locale.
reach: the inbox, every notification producer.

## What happens

`plugin-approvals` already emits `keyedText`. `service-messaging` renders it per recipient at delivery (`notification-text.ts`, `NotificationTextRenderer`: the recipient's `sys_user.locale`, else the deployment default). The inbox channel (`inbox-channel.ts`) writes only the rendered `title` / `body_md` onto `sys_inbox_message`. That object has no field holding the keys (`inbox-message.object.ts`: id, user_id, notification_id, delivery_id, actor_id, topic, title, body_md, severity, action_url, created_at). The keys survive only in the durable outbox snapshot (`sys_notification_delivery.payload.keyedText`), and the inline fan-out path stores none. A reader whose request locale differs from the stored one therefore always gets the delivery-time language.

## Expected

The inbox composes a keyed title and body in the reader's request locale at read time, as `plugin-audit`'s `sys_activity` summary middleware does. Rows written before the change keep their stored text.

## Seat's direction (from #32218's thread, recommended option A)

- **A (recommended):** store the keys on `sys_inbox_message` (a new read-only field) at delivery on both the durable and inline paths, plus a read middleware on that object that re-renders title and body in the request locale when keys are present. It covers every producer. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on a published object.
- B: a read middleware that joins inbox rows to their delivery snapshot by `delivery_id`. This works on the durable path only, costs one extra read per page, and is not recommended.
